headline: A Bradford NHS hospital says an AI skin-lesion checker lets it see a third more patients per clinic session.
score_reason: Concrete local results, but early, trust-reported and vendor-claimed accuracy.
importance_line: Skin-cancer patients in Bradford may be seen sooner and have fewer unneeded biopsies, but the figures come from the hospital trust and the maker, and a clinician still checks every image.
summary: The BBC reports that St Luke's Hospital in Bradford, which adopted the DERM AI system in April, now sees 32 patients per skin clinic session instead of 24, and the trust says unnecessary biopsies have fallen by about 10%. The maker, Skin Analytics, claims 99.9% accuracy at ruling out melanoma; the BBC says every image is double-checked by a clinician and the NHS evidence review runs for three years.
